content.comment_body: Hello everyone, just a quick heads-up that took my IT team several days to resolve. After updating Chrome/Edge to version 124, I could no longer reach the extended webserver of my [product_name]. The connection was immediately terminated, and the browser indicated a missing security certificate. This wasn't an error with the [product_name], but rather a result of the Chrome/Edge update, which activated an extra security feature for TLS 1.3. If you experience a similar issue, search online for "quantum-resistant X25519Kyber768 issue" to find temporary solutions. It is expected that this will be fully resolved eventually through a device/root certificate update by [company_name].
Have you reached out to [company_name] to ask if they plan to fix this? Do you know if it impacts units with [version_no]?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering problems accessing the web server of a [company_name] [product_name] with Chrome and Edge browsers following a recent browser update. The main issue is sudden connection failure and a missing certificate notice, attributed to enhanced browser security settings enforcing stricter TLS 1.3 and quantum-resistant cipher requirements. Users are unclear whether the error stems from the device and are uncertain about [company_name]'s response time and which hardware versions are affected.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the web server on their [product_name] devices to remain accessible, regardless of browser updates, and hope that [company_name] will resolve certificate compatibility problems through prompt device/root certificate updates.
